answer.evidence: The main rack body (rows 8-20, 30 px wide) has a shelf band in rows 9-15. It is striped with rails (x=16 alternates L 111/91/169/91/169/91) and ends in a light front-edge line at row 15 (L 202-224). Row 16 is a dark line that acts as eave shadow, and the front face is the silver panel in rows 17-19 with the dark outline at row 20. The two bags sit on the shelf and count as decor. The four small cards in rows 23-29 are separate flat items hanging below, joined only by a 2 px connector in rows 21-22. I treated them as decor, which is a judgment call because they could also be read as a separate object. The top is a 7-row shelf, not just a rim, so the rack reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a shelf with a few bags and suitcases and small tags underneath. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral near-black line like the lamp-crook's. The richer references (stall, well, hedge) have tinted outlines at 0-33% neutral. Each material on the candidate (grey shelf, bag bodies, suitcase) has about 2-3 steps, a body tone plus a highlight and an outline, against about 5 steps on the stall and well. The measured facts do not count against it: 11 visible tones per tile is above the hedge's 9 but below the stall's 17 and the well's 20, and near-flat coverage is 0%. The objects still read as flat-shaded shapes with little grain or per-item shading, which gives a sticker look beside the stall and well. Because of the neutral outline and shallow ramps, it would look thinner than the references.

answer.evidence: The rack is drawn almost flat-on. The outer frame (rows 8-20) is a front-facing rectangle with a 30px silhouette. The shelf has only a 2-row light band (rows 14-15) ending in a dark line at row 16, then a front face at rows 17-19. That is a rim-sized top of 2 rows, not a real horizontal surface. The back rail area at rows 9-13 is vertical, with no ellipse or contents showing as a top. The suitcase and bag are decor sitting on the shelf. The four small panels at rows 23-29 are separate flat front-view items that add no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small rack with a dark-blue bag, a beige bag and white tags. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral near-black line rather than a dark tint of the neighbouring material. The Beodeul stall, well and hedge references are 0-33% neutral. The lamp-crook reference is also 100% neutral, but it is a thin metal pole, which is not a fair comparison for a multi-material prop. Each material (grey frame, bags, tags) has only about 2-3 tones, and the bags read as near-flat blocks with one highlight each. By the numbers, the candidate has 11 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage. That is above the hedge (9) but well below the well (20) and stall (17), which carry grain, per-part shading and material-tone outlines. There are no large flat fills, but the shading is shallow and the neutral outline gives it a sticker look next to the references. It is not up to the Beodeul bar.
